page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It features 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, translating to 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance is equipped with a 75 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps under the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations indicate mixed performance characteristics. Single-core capabilities are moderate, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the average range. However, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests, fall into the bottom 10% tier. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor performance, with large block read and write operations categorized in the bottom 25%. Static web serving and database operations also register in the lower 10% performance bracket.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c5ad.large offers a dedicated compute resource profile with high-speed local NVMe storage at a lower entry-level resource density. The inclusion of local SSD storage offsets the lower memory-to-vCPU ratio for specific workloads. This instance is suited for lightweight compute tasks, basic single-threaded processing, software compilation, and development environments that benefit from fast local scratch space but do not require high memory capacity or sustained multi-core performance.
